OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS

  Regular Meeting at 8:30 AM
  Cafe Wang Restaurant
  2316 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750
Attendance and participation at the Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District meetings are
welcomed and appreciated. Community engagement provides the Committee with valuable
information. In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City
Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

Persons addressing the Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District shall be limited to 3
minutes unless an extension of time is granted by the Chair, subject to approval of the Committee
Members. When any group of persons wishes to address the Committee, it shall be proper for the
Chair to request that a spokesperson be chosen to represent the group.

Public comments will be allowed on items on this Agenda at the time each item is considered.

CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

PRESENTATIONS

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

1.  Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District Minutes of the Regular meeting of
  February 2, 2026. Approval of Minutes.
  Recommendation: That the Advisory Board approve the minutes of the Regular meeting of
  February 2, 2026.

DISCUSSION ITEMS

2.  Budget Overview The draft 2026-2027 Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District
  budget will be presented to the Advisory Board for review and recommendation.

  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, February 2, 2026

1. WELCOME AND CALL TO ORDER

  The meeting began at 8:43 a.m.

  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Micky Rehm and George Henderson.
  Advisory Board Members not present: Zuhey Espinoza and Marianne Stark.
  City Representatives present: Mayor Tim Hepburn, City Manager Ken Domer,
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer, Public Works Director Danny Wu,
  Senior Management Analyst Nicole Houston, Maintenance Manager Ramiro Nunez,
  Maintenance Supervisor Richard Casados, and Secretary Natalie Hiatt. Others present:
  Fang Wang, Ken Valmonte, Francisco Ramirez, and Roy Cannizzo.

2. CALENDAR
  Cool Cruise Car Show  Saturday, April 4th 9am-3pm
  Wine Walk  Saturday, April 18th 5pm-8:30pm

3. APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES November 3, 2025

  It was moved by Mr. Henderson and seconded by Ms. Rehm to approve the minutes of
  November 3, 2025. Minutes approved by a 3-0 vote.

4. NEW BUSINESS

  A. Holiday Stroll Recap – Chairperson Walters stated that Holiday Stroll was expanded
  to include a street closure on 3rd Street to include vendors and a petting zoo. The
  event was well attended but also more costly.
  B. Wine Walk Update – Ms. Rehm stated that the first Wine Walking meeting was held
  last week. Event planner Sheila Rodriguez is taking the lead on planning the event.
  The committee decided to reduce the ticket price by $5 and will also offer early bird
  pricing. The committee is still undecided on this year’s charity. The application
  period will run from February 15th through March 15th.
  C. Tree Light Improvements – Chairperson Walter detailed ongoing issues with the
  current tree lights and the need to reevaluate the options.

  Mr. Wu introduced his staff. They stated in February 2025 they received an
  assessment which included options for repairing and replacing electrical and an
  arborists report. It was recommended by Mr. Ken Domer to research other local cities
  for ideas. Ms. Rehm and Mr. Henderson also suggested stringing lights across the

  Page 3 of 8
   street. Mr. Casados stated there is concern that the current power on Bonita Avenue is
  not enough for a tree light expansion. It is likely that a new pedestal would be needed.

  Ms. Rehm requested that the trash receptacles be emptied more often to prevent
  overfilling over the weekend. Mr. Scherer stated that it’s currently being emptied on
  Monday and Thursday.

5. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. Sidewalk Use Permit – Mr. Scherer stated that not all businesses are in compliance.
  Mr. Domer sent a reminder email on Friday and beginning in one week Public Works
  will do a sweep and remove items.
  B. Walk of Honor Update – Chairperson Walters stated that the committee is in the
  process of becoming a 501(c)(3) organization. The group’s intent is to recognize 10
  people per year.

6. COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A. City Report (Eric Scherer): Mr. Scherer stated that a filming request was received that
  would require a street closure on D Street. The requestor identified February 25th as a
  possible date. Mr. Domer and Mr. Scherer both stated that more information is
  needed and City Council approval is required. Ms. Rehm suggested filming on a
  Monday would be better as many businesses are already closed that day.
  B. University Report: (Zuhey Espinoza): None
  C. Chamber Report: None
  D. Financial Report: The Association board met with Mr. Scherer, Mr. Domer,
  Councilmember Lau, and Mayor Hepburn last week. There was an agreement to
  transfer $60,000 from the reserve account to the Association to fund future events.
  After the transfer the Association will receive no further assistance from the reserve
  account.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the City Council is in favor of continuing the car shows and
  the organizer fee will be paid from the District account. Mr. Scherer requested the
  organizer provide more information on the event finances before an agreement is
  made. Ms. Rehm expressed concern that the organizer is talking badly of the City and
  merchants.

  Chairperson Walters explained that the Association’s responsibility is to promote and
  market Old Town and the District is responsible for overseeing the operations.

  Mr. Scherer requested that a budget sub-committee meet before the next BID
  meeting. Chairperson Walters and Ms. Rehm volunteered for the sub-committee.

7. PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  Page 4 of 8
   Mr. Cannizzo inquired why a Chamber representative isn’t present. Mr. Scherer
  stated that Mr. Duran attended the November meeting.

  Ms. Rehm expressed concern with a protestor in Old Town. Mr. Domer
  recommended calling the Police Department if he is harassing people. Mr. Domer
  will discuss it more with the City Attorney.

8. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:39am, the next regular meeting to be held on May 4,
  2026 at 8:30 a.m. at Café Wang – 2316 D Street, La Verne CA 91750.

  Respectively submitted,

  _____________________
  Natalie Hiatt

DATE:  May 4, 2026
TO:  Honorable Chair and Committee Members
FROM:  Eric Scherer, Community Development Director
SUBJECT:  BUDGET OVERVIEW

SUMMARY
The draft 2026-2027 Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District budget will be
presented to the Advisory Board for review and recommendation.

RECOMMENDATION
That the Advisory Board recommend that the City Council adopt the draft budget for the Old
Town La Verne Business Improvement District as a part of the budget process.

DISCUSSION
As approved by the City Council in 2025, the non-profit Old Town La Verne Business
Improvement Association (“Association”) now acts as the District’s Advisory Board, and all
events were transferred to the Association for their budgeting. The City continues to budget for
the District’s ongoing maintenance and capital improvement projects with the revenues
collected from the annual assessments.

During the 2025-2026 fiscal year, the Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District
(“District”) received approximately $22,500 from the District assessments paid by the
businesses within the District. The expenditures for the District’s budget this fiscal year are
projected to be $14,500. However, for the transition of events to the Association during this
fiscal year, a one-time transfer of approximately $68,600 was paid to the Association from
District reserves. The anticipated fund balance on July 1, 2026 is expected to be approximately
$115,500.

The 2026-2027 annual budget has projected expenditures of approximately $17,200, with
projected revenues of $25,000, leaving a fund balance of $123,300 at the end of the next year.
A summary of the proposed 2026-2027 budget is attached.

FISCAL ANALYSIS
The recommended budget has District revenues exceeding expenditures, which will result in
additional funds going to reserves. These reserves will eventually be programed for a capital
improvement project once a study is completed by a consultant.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
None.

CITY OF LA VERNE
  OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS
  IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT
  MINUTES
  May 4, 2026 - 8:30 AM
  Cafe Wang Restaurant
  2316 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was relocated to Warehouse Pizza located at 2340 D Street. The meeting began at 8:36 a.m.

ROLL CALL
Advisory Board Members present: Zuhey Espinoza, Micky Rehm, Marianne Stark, and Craig Walters
Advisory Board Members not present: George Henderson
City Representatives present: Mayor Tim Hepburn, Community Development Director Eric Scherer, and
Administrative Specialist Natalie Hiatt
Others Present: Francisco Ramirez, Roy Cannizzo, and Kenny Schonfield

PRESENTATIONS
None

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

1.  Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District Minutes of the Regular meeting of
  February 2, 2026.
  Recommendation: That the Advisory Board approve the minutes of the Regular meeting of
  February 2, 2026.
It was moved by Ms. Rehm and seconded by Ms. Stark to approve the minutes of the February 2, 2026 meeting.
Motion carried by a 4-0 vote (Henderson absent).

DISCUSSION ITEMS

2.  Budget Overview The draft 2026-2027 Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District
  budget will be presented to the Advisory Board for review and recommendation.
  Recommendation: That the Advisory Board recommend that the City Council adopt the draft
  budget for the Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District as a part of the budget
  process.
Committee Discussion/Comments: The group stated that they are not in favor of funding the car show with
District funds.

Chairperson Walters suggested an increase to the BID fees.

Mr. Scherer stated that the City Council is in support of the car show as it is a community event.
 There was a discussion regarding adding wayfinding parking signs.

Mayor Hepburn also suggested cleaning up the park in front of Warehouse Pizza.

Chairperson Walters suggested that funds be used for small upgrades such as signs and adding additional trash
cans.

It was moved by Ms. Stark and seconded by Ms. Rehm to remove Cool Cruise from the budget and move $5,000 to
operational improvements. The motion carried by a 4-0 (Henderson absent).

PUBLIC COMMENT
Public comments will be allowed on items not on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction
of the Committee; however, no action may be taken on off-agenda items except as provided by law.
Mayor Hepburn stated that the Wine Walk check-in lines were long but otherwise it was a great event.

Mr. Cannizzo stated his concerns regarding trash pickup by Waste Management.

STAFF/COMMITTEE COMMUNICATION & INFORMATION
Committee members may ask a question for clarification, make a brief announcement, make a brief
report on his/her own activities, request staff to report back at a subsequent meeting concerning any
matter, or take action to direct staff to place a matter of business on a future agenda.
Ms. Espinoza discussed the University's Gala event and stated that one-hundred percent of the proceeds are used
for scholarships. She announced that Risa Dickson was voted to serve as the permanent President, the University
will revisit the Master Plan, Congressman Gil Cisneros held the Congressional Art Competition for local high
school kids at the University, and commencement will take place on May 30th.

Chairperson Walters stated that 1,015 Wine Walk tickets were sold. The Holiday Stroll will be held on December
1st and the next Walk of Honor recipients will be presented.

Mr. Scherer stated that the City is in support of the group's events. He stated there was a question raised
regarding the City's installation of the Walk of Honor plaques. The City Manager will follow-up with more
information regarding a new policy.

Ms. Rehm announced that the Beer Walk event will be held on September 19th.

ADJOURNMENT
The meeting was adjourned at 9:35 a.m., the next regular meeting to be held on August 3, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. at
Cafe Wang - 2316 D Street, La Verne CA 91750.

Respectfully submitted,

Natalie Hiatt, Secretary
